title: D2606019 (R.23-02-016) Order Extending Statutory Deadline
text:
ALJ/TJG/jds/vj4 Date of Issuance 6/19/2026
Decision 26-06-019 June 11, 2026
BEFORE THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA
Order Instituting Rulemaking
Proceeding to Consider Rules to
Implement the Broadband Equity, Rulemaking 23-02-016
Access, and Deployment Program.
ORDER EXTENDING STATUTORY DEADLINE
Summary
This decision extends the statutory deadline in this proceeding to
October 30, 2026.
1. Background
Public Utilities Code (Pub. Util. Code) Section 1701.5(a) provides that the
Commission shall resolve the issues raised in the scoping memo of a quasi-
legislative proceeding within 18 months of the date the proceeding is initiated,
unless the Commission makes a written determination that the deadline cannot
be met and issues an order extending that deadline. The current statutory
deadline for completion of Rulemaking (R.) 23-02-016 is June 30, 2026.
On February 23, 2023, the California Public Utilities Commission
(Commission), on its own motion, opened R.23-02-016 to consider rules to
determine grant funding, eligibility and compliance for funds distributed to
California under the federal Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment
609222815 - 1 -

R.23-02-016 ALJ/TJG/jds/vj4
(BEAD) Program, created by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA)
of 2021. Among the law’s numerous provisions, the IIJA establishes the $42.45
billion BEAD Program, administered by the National Telecommunications and
Information Administration (NTIA). After receiving BEAD funding from the
NTIA, a state was allowed to award sub-grants competitively to subgrantees to
carry out the following broadband deployment activities: 1) unserved service
projects; 2) underserved service projects; 3) projects connecting eligible
community anchor institutions; 4) broadband data collection, mapping, and
planning; 5) installing internet and Wi-Fi infrastructure or providing reduced-
cost broadband within a multi-family residential building; 6) broadband
adoption programs; and 7) other activities determined by NTIA.
On April 11, 2023, the Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) issued a ruling
providing notice of public engagement workshops. The Commission and the
California Department of Technology (CDT) partnered with local and regional
organizations and other state entities to host 20 BEAD planning workshops
throughout the state. The Governor designated the Commission to serve as the
recipient of and administering agent for the BEAD program for California and
designated the CDT to serve as the recipient of and administering agent for the
Digital Equity Plan. These workshops were conducted from April 14, 2023, to
June 2, 2023. On May 3, 2023, the ALJ issued a ruling providing notice of two
additional public engagement workshops.
On April 17, 2023, parties filed comments in response to the R.23-02-016.
On May 8, 2023, parties filed reply comments
- 2 -

R.23-02-016 ALJ/TJG/jds/vj4
On May 18, 2023, the ALJ issued a ruling setting a prehearing conference
(PHC) for May 31, 2023, to address the issues of law and fact, determine the need
for hearing, set the schedule for resolving the matter, and address other matters
as necessary.
On July 14, 2023, Commissioner Darie L. Houck issued a Scoping Memo
and Ruling, setting the proceeding schedule and placing the following issues
within the scope of this proceeding: Extremely High-Cost Threshold, Geographic
Level, Overlapping Project Areas, Selection Among Priority Broadband Projects,
Selection Among Other Last-Mile Broadband Deployment Projects, Challenge
Process, Match Requirement, Statewide Middle Mile, Ministerial Review,
Affordability, Technical Assistance, Climate Resilience, Labor Practices and
Workforce Development, Grant Conditions, Grant Applications, Payments and
Impacts on Environmental and Social Justice Communities.
On July 17, 2023, the ALJ issued a ruling that provided a draft BEAD
Program Five-Year Action Plan for party comment.
On September 27, 2023, the ALJ issued a ruling setting two Public
Participation Hearings (PPHs) to be held on November 8, 2023.
On October 13, 2023, the ALJ issued a ruling noticing a workshop to be
held on October 26, 2023.
On November 7, 2023, the ALJ issued a ruling to serve proposed rules for
the BEAD Program for party comment.
On April 4, 2024, the ALJ issued a ruling noticing NTIA curing instructions
regarding the Commission’s Initial Proposal Volume 1 for the BEAD Program.
- 3 -

R.23-02-016 ALJ/TJG/jds/vj4
On April 5, 2024, Commissioner Houck issued a proposed decision
approving Volume 1 of the BEAD Program Rules.
On August 22, 2024, Decision (D.) 24-08-050 extended the statutory
deadline for this proceeding to June 30, 2026.
On December 19, 2025, the Commission submitted to the NTIA its Final
Proposal for the BEAD Program. The NTIA has not yet approved the
Commission’s Final Proposal, and without an NTIA-approved Final Proposal,
R.23-02-016 cannot be completed before June 30, 2026. Consequently, an
extension of the statutory deadline to October 30, 2026, is appropriate to allow
the Commission sufficient time to resolve this proceeding.
2. Waiver of Comment Period
Under Rule 14.6(c)(4) of the Commission’s Rules, the Commission may
waive the otherwise applicable 30-day period for public review and comment on
a decision that extends the 18-month deadline set forth in Pub. Util. Code Section
1701.5. Under the circumstances of this proceeding, it is appropriate to waive the
30-day period for public review and comment.
3. Assignment of Proceeding
Darcie L. Houck is the assigned Commissioner and Thomas J. Glegola is
the assigned Administrative Law Judge in this proceeding.
Findings of Fact
1. R.23-02-016 was filed on February 23, 2023.
2. Public engagement workshops were conducted from April 14, 2023, to
June 2, 2023.
3. A PHC was held on May 31, 2023.
- 4 -

R.23-02-016 ALJ/TJG/jds/vj4
4. On July 14, 2023, a scoping memo and ruling was issued to consider
numerous issues regarding the BEAD Program.
5. On July 17, 2023, a draft BEAD Program Five-Year Action Plan was
provided for party comment.
6. On November 8, 2023, two PPHs were held.
7. On April 5, 2024, the assigned Commissioner issued a proposed decision
approving Volume 1 of the BEAD Program Rules.
8. On August 22, 2024, D.24-08-050 extended the statutory deadline for
R.23-02-016 to June 30, 2026.
9. R.23-02-016 cannot be completed by June 30, 2026.
10. An extension of the statutory deadline to October 30, 2026, is appropriate
to allow the Commission sufficient time to resolve this proceeding.
Conclusion of Law
1. Pursuant to the authority granted to the Commission under Pub.
Util. Code § 1701.5(a), the statutory deadline in this proceeding should be
extended to October 30, 2026.
IT IS ORDERED that the statutory deadline in this proceeding is extended
until October 30, 2026.
This order is effective today.
Dated June 11, 2026, at Sacramento, California.
